entries.claim: The legacy engine text contains both a turn-one draw skip rule and an older draw expectation; acceptance also describes automatic draw on a later turn.
entries.evidence: Current runtime and review tests must be treated as evidence, but the reset brief supplies no explicit ruling that resolves every wording variant.
entries.decision: Do not change runtime or assert a new semantic in an active contract. Preserve the conflict in the archive until an explicit ruling and current green evidence agree.

entries.claim: Opening hand, cleanup maximum, and older UI descriptions use 7/8-card language in different contexts.
entries.evidence: Opening setup is described as seven cards while cleanup behavior and older UI material mention eight; the reset brief forbids guessing between them.
entries.decision: Keep the contexts separate in migration data and do not rewrite runtime behavior. Any remaining ambiguous scenario is not active-green.

entries.claim: Legacy Playmat and current GameScreen descriptions coexist with mobile/desktop acceptance language.
entries.evidence: The current README carries both deleted-file history and current UI claims; acceptance still contains legacy interaction wording.
entries.decision: Move lineage and audit material to archive/ADR. Active UI contracts describe only current principles and interfaces; no product UI change is made.

entries.claim: Normal acceptance mixes fixed fixtures with live Scryfall verification.
entries.evidence: The brief explicitly assigns fixed fixture/snapshot data to normal acceptance and live Scryfall to online/periodic lanes.
entries.decision: Active scenarios use fixed fixtures; live API checks are periodic/online only.

entries.claim: Older acceptance text requires full scenario replay after any failure.
entries.evidence: The reset brief supplies the replacement scenario/domain/wide-lane rules.
entries.decision: Use scenario-from-start, shared-fixture domain, shared-infrastructure wide-domain, and candidate-freeze release rules.

entries.claim: The release workflow builds once inside check and once again for Pages.
entries.evidence: The workflow runs npm run check followed by npm run build -- --base=/MTG_OneDeck/.
entries.decision: Parameterize the single release build and upload that dist artifact.

entries.claim: The default forbidden scan uses only a clean checkout's git status.
entries.evidence: The script defaults to git status --short and the workflow invokes it without a base/diff argument.
entries.decision: Require the workflow to pass an explicit base ref/diff while retaining status mode for local worktrees.

entries.claim: The same three Solo-preservation test files are run by a dedicated step and again by full DOM Vitest.
entries.evidence: The baseline output shows a dedicated 3-file run before the full core/dom suite.
entries.decision: Keep the dedicated check in fast/domain lanes; in release, let the full Vitest run own those files once.
